Content: Hey there, {PlayerName}. It's been a while, huh?
You're out of the Xuanyuan Domain?
Drop the act, Ruoyun.
You got out of the Xuanyuan Domain, Jadie? How did you get my contact info?
Well, just some techs. Easy peasy.
Drop the act, Ruoyun.
Shh... It's Jadie, okay?
I came out for some air a while back, but I'm back in the Xuanyuan Domain now.
There's still so much cleanup work to do.
And you contacted me because...
So you contacted me because... you need my help with something?
Why would I? Of course it's because... I've got an important picture for you!
Sent a copy to Qingxiao too. She seemed pretty happy after seeing it.
Care to explain?
Care to explain? How did you get your hands on that picture?
Well, that's a secret. We got to have a keepsake for such a moment, right?
Well... if you don't have anything else to ask, I'll get going now. See you!
Friend has gone offline.
It seems the mountain gate does not open from this side...

...

The beacon fires of the Fortress and Gorges War at last burned low, and peace was restored across the realms.

Mingting issued a proclamation, calling upon the full might of Huanglong to raise a new fortified city south of the Central Plains and naming it Jinzhou. Thenceforth, the lands east of the Mountains of Spirits and south of the Norfall Barrens fell under Jinzhou's jurisdiction.

The first Magistrate of Jinzhou decreed that the city would bear no emblem of its own. Instead, it would share the insignia of Huanglong, in remembrance of the bond forged in aid with the one capital and five cities.

...
I completely forgot about it. Yuan Fortress's mountain gate is still under maintenance.
These shipments will just have to wait, I guess...
Wait... Is that Qingxiao the Transcendent I'm seeing?
Heard there's always a Xuanling Bird next to her, but I didn't see one just now.
Maybe it wasn't the Xuanling Bird who asked her to come down the mountain this time?
Besides us, did the Gorges of Spirits get hit by the TD Outbreak too?
Yeah. Heard the Threnodian hit hardest there. Even the Crownless showed up.
Besides us, did the Gorges of Spirits get hit by the TD Outbreak too?
Yeah. Heard the Threnodian hit hardest there. Even the Crownless showed up.
Splitting up to hit both fronts and cut off communication between us. Crafty bastard.
True. As long as the Gorges of Spirits are still in a mess, the Threnodian's gonna keep sending TDs our way.
If it weren't for the Cloud Shuttles, this battle would've gone a whole different way...
Don't dwell on it. Truth is, you and I barely set foot out there, and it was nearly over.
I came to Yuan Fortress to learn how Cloud Shuttles are manufactured.
Well, not down here you won't. You'll need to find a way to go up there.
You mean... on a Cloud Shuttle?
That's right. You can apply for a Cloud Shuttle maintenance team someday.
The passage this side is undergoing maintenance. Please stand clear.
Road. Maintenance. Closed.
My stomach just turns every time the Cloud Shuttle takes off...
Oh, I've got my own problem... I'm scared of heights. My legs are shaking already.
Spend enough time up in the air and we'll get used to it.
Is it just me, or are there more TDs showing up around lately?
Let's keep an eye on this. We'll report any confirmed anomalies to the Ministry of War.
This large sphere... Is that the control kernel of the Cloud Shuttle?
Right you are. It's also the power source that propels the Cloud Shuttle during its flight.
This large sphere... Is that the control kernel of the Cloud Shuttle?
Right you are. It's also the power source that propels the Cloud Shuttle during its flight.
I can hardly imagine how it manages to support the Cloud Shuttle's operations. How does it even work?
I'm not entirely sure either. It must be one of those "miracles" of mechanist arts.
What happens if it breaks down one day?
Don't worry. They've been around since forever, and I've never heard of any Cloud Shuttle's kernel having problems.
Never expected we'd meet on a Cloud Shuttle. How are things over at Zhuojun Atelier?
Can't complain. Lot more freedom than back at the Ministry of Development. Fewer hoops to jump through when you're doing research.
Never expected we'd meet on a Cloud Shuttle. How are things over at Zhuojun Atelier?
Can't complain. Lot more freedom than back at the Ministry of Development. Fewer hoops to jump through when you're doing research.
So what's this about, old friend? Here to check up on me for the Ministry?
Don't be ridiculous. Up here on the Cloud Shuttle, we're all just maintenance crew. Nobody's keeping tabs on anybody.
Fair enough. Looking forward to working together again.
Come on, spit it out. How did you get on board the Cloud Shuttle?
Well... I hid inside a cargo crate when the Cloud Shuttle was refueling. Haha...
All right, I think you've seen enough. I'll have the Ministry of War take care of you once we land.
Wait, wait, please, ma'am. Can't you just let this one slide? I'll be gone before you even know it.
The mechanisms run on their own anyway. A little extra rest won't hurt...
The scenery here is really breathtaking. And the breeze is so nice...
Say, which one do you think is faster? The Sword Transcendent's flying sword? Or the Cloud Shuttle?
Probably the flying sword. The last time I saw the Sword Transcendent, she whizzed past like a beam of light.
Wait, wasn't that the Sword Transcendent just now?
... Someone must've altered my memories.
Who exactly is controlling me to stay on the Cloud Shuttle?
We should form a patrol team soon to help ease the burden on the Ministry of War.
Quite a few of the young folks in the village have already brought up the idea. They're just waiting on your word.
Listen up, everyone, we're well ahead of the maintenance schedule for the day. So we all get early rest.
Why's he talking to empty space...?
We should form a patrol team soon to help ease the burden on the Ministry of War.
Quite a few of the young folks in the village have already brought up the idea. They're just waiting on your word.
I'll get them together later. At least we'll be ready next time the TDs show up.
I'll join you. Say, remember that heavy downpour years ago?
Of course. If the Rafter Kite hadn't brought Paragon Qingxiao at the time, us kids would've been swept away in the flood.
The village really owes her for her protection all these years.
That lightway in the distance connects to a higher region beyond.
How do you know? Have you been there?
That lightway in the distance connects to a higher region beyond.
How do you know? Have you been there?
I don't quite remember, but yeah, I have been there.
The place's gloomy. The sky is nowhere near as clear as it is here. And they have so many Cloud Shuttles running as well...
The Cloud Shuttle's control kernel seems to be spinning at an abnormal rate...
Old Qian! I-I want to join the patrol. We all ought to do our part for our home.
Oh, you old fool. You're still nursing a bad leg. Don't go making trouble for everyone.
I spoke with Commander Qiuhong. We can start by organizing the villagers ourselves.
The Xuanfang Wardens need to focus on the defenses. Let's spare them the trouble where we can.
The Ministry of War doesn't have enough beds for everyone, so we'll need to set some up in the courtyard.
Same as last time. The elderly, the frail, and the wounded get indoors first. I'll be sleeping outside tonight as well.
Is it true that both the Skywatch Rings and the Mingshen System went down?
Yes, now we can only rely on Rafter Kites to scout the surrounding area.
Is it true that both the Skywatch Rings and the Mingshen System went down?
Yes, now we can only rely on Rafter Kites to scout the surrounding area.
Look on the bright side. At least this time the Autopuppets aren't our enemies anymore.
But the Autopuppets can't help us either. Setting up defensive lines is much harder than it used to be.
In any case, we're on our own now. Hop to it.
A lot of folks haven't had a chance to eat. We should prep some snacks later.
Sounds good. We should borrow some utensils from the Fillet Fairmaiden.
So, what did the Commander mean by "we must fall back, line by line"?
Basically, we set up several defense lines around the perimeter, and put most of our manpower on the spots that matter most.
So it means... the area around the Ministry of War is our final stronghold?
Ugh, if I hadn't gotten careless and let that TD swipe at me, I'd be out there helping build the defenses right now.
The TDs were literally by our door back then. What were you doing rummaging through the home?
What could possibly be worth more than your life? What if you get left behind for missing the evacuation?
Ah, it's just an old habit I can't shake. Don't worry, I won't do it again.
Well, I certainly hope there won't be another evacuation...
These are volatile times. Please remain inside the Ministry of War.
For your safety, this area is now off-limits. Sorry for the inconvenience.
Defense preparations are proceeding on schedule. Take a rest, everyone. No need to worry.
Paragon Qingxiao, {PlayerName}, I wish you both a safe journey.
Paragon Qingxiao, {PlayerName}, I wish you both a safe journey.
As things stand, even Lady Hsin's residence may not be called safe. Do take the utmost care.
Take care, sir.
Don't worry. We have Ms. Yangyang and all the soldiers keeping watch. We'll be fine.
The Land of Xuanfang has weathered countless calamities, yet the will of our ancestors endures through the generations. I have faith that things will turn out for the best.
And so—thousands of swords pierced the heavens, scattering the darkness.
The ominous force over Xuanfang was swept away. Mechanisms whirred back to life, and Tacet Discords were locked away.
Above the Sanctum, it seemed as though a river of stars had descended.
As the dust settled, the righteous returned in triumph.
Soldier and citizen cheered as one. Peace, at last, filled the city once more.
Yet before the sounds of celebration had faded, a certain garden collapsed without warning.
As for the secrets it buried... that shall be a tale for another time.
...Thank goodness you're both safe. Yangyang, come closer and let me get a good look at you. Are you hurt?
Suisui, I really am fine... {PlayerName} and Paragon Qingxiao are the ones who went into the Sanctum. They faced all the real danger.
Yangyang didn't miss a single beat out there.
She's become one of Xuanfang's bulwarks now.
{PlayerName}, please don't praise me like that in front of my sister...
Alright, alright. Enough flattery, you two. Let's talk business. I'm speaking as Chairwoman of the Zhaoming Commerce Guild now.
After returning to Mengzhou, I used the Guild's connections to dig into Muyu's past and contacted the main branch of Zhuojun Atelier.
Muyu was a prodigy in Automata Mechanics. He designed Yuan Fortress two centuries ago, was a senior figure in Zhuojun Atelier, and had deep collaborations with Huaxu Academy.
About twenty years back, he was supposed to succeed the Flowerveil Puppet as the next Grand Helm. Instead, he announced his departure from the organization and vanished.
After that... he probably hid in Xuanfang under another identity. Biding his time. Refining his plan.
The Atelier has officially cut ties with him. They even offered to share information to help with the Guild's investigation.
But we know he was still receiving internal support through an informant. Oh, right, did you meet the Cat of the Nether Lamp?
(Tell Suisui about Jingran.)
...Really? So he hasn't been seen since the Sanctum... Typical. A proper ghost of the Jianghu. I wouldn't be surprised if he just shows up again one day.
I'm sure he also made it out safely.
But did Muyu have dealings with the Fractsidus? He mentioned an Overseer's name before we ended him.
We've only got one lead, from the Grand Helm herself. She said Muyu traded technology with the Fractsidus years ago, but the relationship didn't last.
Hard to say if that's true or just the Atelier trying to cover its tracks.
These past few days... besides investigating the Atelier, I also made a trip to Mengzhou City Hall.
You went there again...?
Hmph. In Jinzhou, at least they served me tea while I waited. This time... they shut the door in my face. Said Mengzhou's Magistrate wasn't receiving visitors.
Xuanfang's been hit by one disaster after another, yet City Hall remains eerily quiet. It's suspicious.
At least it has made good on its promise: a group of personnel and supplies will arrive from Mengzhou City soon. Another shipment of aid from Jinzhou has also arrived.
Things are indeed looking up. You two needn't worry about City Hall, I'll think of something.
Thank you, Suisui.
Your tone betrays you, darling. I can tell there's a lot on your mind. But you'll try to unwind, won't you?
Yeah... Things are peaceful in Xuanfang for now.
I hope that won't change for a long, long time.
Very soon, the Waking Moon Festival will be celebrated across Mengzhou. Xuanfang will be no exception. You should both take the chance to relax.
Well then, see you soon. Don't forget about our... "next time," alright, {PlayerName}?
{PlayerName}, what did my sister mean by "next time"...?
...One day, we're all gonna visit Jinzhou together.
I'd like that.
Friend sent a nudge
Friend sent a nudge
{PlayerName}, I write to you thus: The skies are clear

{PlayerName}, I write to you thus: 
The skies are clear today, the breeze is gentle, and the weather is most pleasant. Since our hurried parting the other day, I have been occupied handling the Tacet Discords. If you have the time, would you care to visit the training hall? There is something important I wish to discuss.
Qingxiao, respectfully
Qingxiao? Isn't this a little too formal?
You don't have to write WavesLine messages like letters. You can just talk normally.
Understood. I only recently learned how to use WavesLine on the Terminal, so I'm still familiarizing myself with the proper etiquette.
It's okay.
It's okay. Now that you've added me, we can chat whenever. You'll get the hang of it.
Thank you.
My training hall is at the summit of the Eastern Xuan Peaks. Are you available?
I'll head over now.
Of course, I'm free. I'll be there in a flash.
Good. I shall be waiting.
No wonder the Fillet Fairmaiden's running around all day. She's hosting Paragon Qingxiao!
Hey, I heard Paragon Qingxiao recently took a disciple. You think it's the one beside her?
Could it be? But {Male=he;Female=she}'s the great hero from Jinzhou!
You're here.
...So this is your training hall?
When I first settled here, it was nothing but an abandoned shack. Over the years, the local folk have helped me repair it of their own accord.
I owe them a great debt. Cultivation may not need worldly comforts, but if I am to found a school, I should at least have a proper training hall.
...Found a school?
I want to open a school here in Xuanfang. Teach others the way of the sword.
So you're really coming down from the mountain after all.
The Sword Transcendent is taking disciples now?
Where are you at with this?
...Still at the very first step. Finding my first disciple.
The first disciple is the foundation, the face the school shows to the world. I must choose with the utmost care.
Well, you did teach me to fly with a sword not long ago. Doesn't that mean...
This is...
A sword talisman. I carved it myself over the last few days. My lifebound Sword Intent lives inside it.
To be my disciple, you must sever worldly ties, cast aside the six desires, and leave karma behind.
And if, in the end, I cannot?
Then by that time, you will have found a Way of your own.
So, now comes the second step, I guess?
I treat you to a meal.
I believe it's called an Initiation Feast. When my master accepted me, she broke years of fasting just to share a meal.
Back in the Xuanyuan Domain, I called you "disciple," yes. And you called me "master." But that journey has already ended.
I have not truly guided you. Your swordcraft already stands on its own. I've no right to claim you as disciple.
So... it must be your choice.
Qingxiao. If you'll have me, then our journey doesn't need to be over.
...Very well.
According to how my own master accepted me, taking on a disciple requires two steps. This shall be the first.
Think of it as a keepsake of our knowing each other... or as a bond between master and disciple. I hope you will take it.
(Accept it solemnly)
Bring along your adorable little friend as well.
"Adorable"... You mean Abby?
Mengzhou Fish in Vinegar—coming right up! Caught from the Luo River just this morning. You won't find fresher!
Mmm, yum-yum-yum-yum-yum!
Blegh! So sour! What's wrong with this fish?!
This was the signature dish of "Yuan's Flavors" in the late Fortress. I received an invitation to eat there once. One bite, and the taste has never left me.
Disciple, would you like to try some?
Before I always saw the people... as those who quietly waited to be protected.
But the truth is, they've always had the heart to protect themselves.
To save for a day, or to save for a lifetime... Neither compares to teaching them the means to save themselves.
So... that's the real reason you're founding a school?
Many years ago, a fellow Cultivator passed through Xuanfang with his disciple during their travels across Huanglong. He came up the mountain to visit me.

Only then did I learn that to solve Temporal Disruption for future generations, he had to set a plan in motion with a "<ano=you>golden-eyed one</ano>" at Mt. Firmament. It cost him dearly. His lifespan was nearly spent.
And yet, he was at total peace. He had a disciple to inherit his legacy, and his teachings were already taking root across the world.
Master Xuanmiao... and Changli?
Even if one can no longer walk their Way, or devote their life to "peace under heaven," there will always be... someone to take their place.
That is the lesson you taught me, not so long ago.
So, as your first and most devoted disciple, it looks like I'll be helping with the teaching too.
...You already have.
To teach the sword is to offer someone a chance to find their own way with it. Even if they never master it, their body and spirit will still become stronger.
Speaking of which, what are you naming the school?
What should I say if someone asks where I've studied?
Well...
Did you hear? That Transcendent lady is incredible! They say she's the master of the greatest martial arts school in the whole wide world!
What's it called again?
Uh, Xuan... Xuanyuan School! Yeah, it's the best in the world!
In that case... Xuanyuan School it shall be.
In this life, we part more than we gather. Nine times out of ten, the world is not as we wish.
But may we, humble as we are, pass the torch, and never cease to rise.
Hm? Did Paragon Qingxiao leave this behind?
...Swordcraft of the Golden-Eyed One?
(Suisui seems to want to discuss something. I'd better head to the Ministry of War and find Yangyang first.)
It's time for me to close up the stall. Until we meet again, dear listeners.

Some time later, Suisui shares with you and Yangyang the intel she has gathered on Muyu in Mengzhou. She also notes that Mengzhou City Hall continues to hold the Land of Xuanfang at an odd, suspicious distance, and says she will keep monitoring its movements from Mengzhou. She hopes you will allow yourself to unwind and relax at the upcoming Waking Moon Festival...

At her mountain training hall, Qingxiao tells you she wants to found her own school, but what she lacks is a first disciple to serve as its foundation. Your journey to the Sanctum may be over, but your time together is not. Qingxiao holds a brief ceremony to formally take you on as her first disciple, presenting you with a sword talisman containing her feelings, then invites you out to share a meal.

After enjoying a plate of Mengzhou Fish in Vinegar, you and Qingxiao stroll through the streets of Xuanfang Hold. She recalls the time Master Xuanmiao once visited with young Changli. Xuanmiao's lifespan was already badly depleted by then, his days numbered, but he had already found someone to carry on after him. Traveling alongside you, Qingxiao has come to understand that same idea of passing the torch forward, and it is why she seeks to found her own school. She hopes that by teaching swordcraft, she can offer others a chance to walk the path of the blade. True to old rumors and the hopes of local children, she names the new school the Xuanyuan School. When you part, you notice an old, weathered sword manual lying quietly on the restaurant table, apparently left behind by Qingxiao. Inside are illustrations of sword techniques you recognize as your own, from long ago.
It's been some time, {PlayerName}. I trust you've been well?
How's your recovery going?
Yangyang mentioned you've already returned to duty.
I have recovered. Yangyang was with me in the last battle, and we made a good team. A few close calls, but we came through unharmed.
But on to pressing matters. Granny Yanshu asked me to pass you a message. She said, "Jing is back. Do you want to see him?"
I see. I think I'll pay them a visit.
The Paragon's report to the Ministry of War mentioned a Nethermancer who has been a great help... That must've been him, right?
Do you know him?
Xianling is a small village. The young ones grow up together. You cannot help but know each other.
Ah, you came. Jing just stopped by to see me.
Hard to say what that boy's been doing all these years. But the Ministry of War sent him an official commendation.
How did he look?
Oh... Not the best. But he flashed that sly grin of his when he saw me.
Back when Sandao and I took him in, he was like a stray cat. Just fire in his belly and wild to the bone.
Didn't happen overnight, but he simmered down eventually. No more talk about Mengzhou. No more talk about throwing his life away for his parents.
...His parents?
Ah, I've said too much. Happens with age. You'd best ask him yourself. He's out in the field by the woods nearby.
Perfect. I have something to return to him anyway.
Here, take this to him, please. Before he vanishes again. He's always had a sweet tooth for these.
(I still have Jingran's Qingfu pendant. It's time to return it.)
Hey, what's that ya got? Smells kinda scrumptious.
This is for someone else. Don't you be getting any ideas.
(Aww—what crummy luck!)
(The pendant is vibrating. He must be close by...)
Hmph. Well, look who's here. Was gonna find you once I wrap things up.
Jingran, your eye...
Huh? Oh, been stayin' up late. Readin' too much. Nothing Huaxu's miracle eyedrops won't fix, though.
Come on, be serious.
You're not fooling anyone.
It's nothing, just told "Mimi" to collect a little extra this time. Not the first time, won't be last. It'll pass.
The boy runs his mouth. If I hadn't jumped in, you'd be down there playing cards with your Shifu already.
Heh, the old lady must've roped you into this. Thanks.
You probably guessed already. This is that old score I told ya 'bout. The one I got with Muyu.
This is where your...
Relax, they're empty.
Couple decades back, Mengzhou had a real bad day. Some of the Atelier's Bladepuppets went haywire. Killed a bunch of folks. Two of 'em were Artisans. My parents.
After that? No family. Nothin'. Ended up on the street. Then Shifu found me, dragged me back here to Xuanfang.

Back then, all I wanted was to sneak into Mengzhou and cut the guts out of whoever did it. But he knocked me around, set me straight. Then he brought me here. Had me build these two graves. Empty ones.
Said, "Kid, worry about moving forward first. You can settle scores when you're older." Ever since, whenever I start to lose my cool, I come here. Just... sit.
A few years later, I went back to Mengzhou to dig into what happened. The patrol records proved it—those Bladepuppets had Reverberation marks on 'em.
So I followed that thread... and it led me right to Muyu.
Guess I can finally tell my folks it's settled. Shame I can't give Shifu a proper thank-you. Face-to-face, I mean.
...Why not?
The old coot made me promise that when he kicks it, no grave, no marker, no nothing. Tch, live clean, die clean. He locked himself away in some Mirage Realm, lamp and all.
Jingran, I think it's time... to give you this back.
Nah, keep it. Call it a souvenir. Thing ain't worth much, and the Resonance Energy stuck to it just burnt out anyway.
I mean, I could charge it up for ya. Maybe... three months. Tops.
Knock off throwing your life away, would you?
Ain't many things in this world I give a crap about. But I gotta say, lately... I've finally met someone interesting.
Looks like the great Nethermancer, the "Cat of the Nether Lamp" himself didn't find any treasure this time. Just ended up losing a trinket.
Don't count my losses yet. I never do a bad deal.
Hmph.
...Already down to my last.
Are those... Reverberations?
They used to be people.
...Must survive... The truth is within reach...
There is still a chance... My path does not end here...
Whoa there. And where d'you think you're slitherin' off to—
Former Helmsmaster of the <te href=800056>Jianshui Branch</te>, Muyu?
Traitor... How did you find me?
Think I read about this in some old storybook. The old <ano=Bingjie>"sacrifice the body, save the spirit"</ano> trick?
You let someone cut you loose from your old shell, then slipped away in the chaos. Clever. Real clever.
But you went and bent your psyche into a Reverberation. You really think I couldn't track that? 'S kinda what I do.
I admit defeat... That core contains data on the Sentinel. Its worth is incalculable...
All I need is time... Just give me a little more time... and the Sentinel's secret will be laid bare...
Two things you got wrong. First? You got nothing to bargain with. Second? Yeah, this thing's nice, but it ain't that nice... not to me.
Hey, remember that Bladepuppet incident in Mengzhou... what, ten, fifteen years back?
Bladepuppet incident... what was that? I... do not recall...
Tch. Amazing the things you big shots forget. Or did your "escape by execution" stunt scramble your brains?
...Just who are you?
Forget it, then. Don't matter.
But you'll remember this. The one who ends you... was just an ordinary peasant from Xuanfang.
...Humanity... could have been... perfect...
You stopped being human a long time ago. Where's the perfect in that?
...Why didn't you stop me? Coulda squeezed him for more info, if you'd wanted.
Matters of revenge, only the wronged can decide.
Besides... his corpse is not without use.
Here. You lot'll put it to better use than me.
What's taking so long... Why isn't the contact here yet? Could the former Helmsmaster's arrangements have gone wrong...?
Don't lose your head. If something has changed, we will simply report to headquarters ourselves.
Aw, didn't see me here?
You're the contact for the Zhijiang Branch?
Spare me the little tricks. You were waiting for the Jianshui Branch. What, do I not look the part?
Uh... "Windingflow Vessel"?
"Hundredfold Assemblage."
Pardon our disrespect. You came at the right time. We have <ano=Muyu>the former Helmsmaster's</ano> manuscripts from his time in Xuanfang, and a recent secret letter.
Top-notch work, fellas. The Grand Helm will definitely know your names after this. No time to waste, you'll be coming with me. Except...
I'm afraid I'll have to restrain you. Just a little.
Why you—?!
Shh. For your own sake, I recommend you save your breath.
Ah... Lady Suoming. What brings you to Xuanfang?
Don't misunderstand. I'm not here for the Atelier's affairs.
The Ministry of Sentinel Affairs governs the Sentinel's business. You being here... Could it be—
You already know all you need to know. Take care.
See you around, {PlayerName}... If we're lucky.
So, you are the Jinzhou Patroller seconded to Mengzhou?
It could be yours... For Nethermancers... No, for Xuanfang, it would mean everything...
Liangyu passes along a message from Granny Yanshu: Jingran is back. You decide to go see him.

Yanshu tells you Jingran stopped by to see her right after he returned, and that the Ministry of War even sent him an official commendation. He is currently out in a clearing in the nearby woods. She asks you to bring him some freshly made pastries.

You find Jingran at a grave in the woods, and he opens up about his past. Years ago, Muyu triggered a Bladepuppet incident in Mengzhou that killed Jingran's parents—the reason he has hunted Muyu ever since. His master took him in when he was a homeless orphan bent on revenge, and taught him that vengeance need not be rushed. Jingran gives you his Qingfu pendant as a memento of your meeting. Together at a cliffside, you help him release the Reverberations of the dead, letting the departed finally find peace.

As the previous crisis draws to a close, Jingran tracks Muyu to a garden somewhere in Xuanfang Hold. Muyu, having fled the last battle in puppet form, seems only a step away from uncovering the Sentinel's secrets. Muyu tries to make him an offer, but Jingran refuses, ending Muyu's life proudly as an ordinary citizen of Xuanfang. He then hands the technology core containing the Sentinel's data to Qiuyuan, who has just arrived in Xuanfang Hold. As the two men part ways, the garden slowly crumbles into ruin...

At the crossroads leading into the heartland of Mengzhou, Yinlin, posing as a contact for Zhuojun Atelier, intercepts intel Muyu was sending to Mengzhou. Meanwhile, Suoming of the Ministry of Sentinel Affairs arrives in Xuanfang, seemingly on business tied to Mengzhou's Sentinel...
Friend sent a nudge
...I accidentally tapped your profile picture again.
Disciple, I find that I neglected to give you a proper initiation gift.
There's more than one?
Oh? I like the sound of that.
What about the sword talisman? There's more than one initiation gift?
Oh? I like the sound of that.
The sword talisman was a symbol of our bond as master and disciple. An inaugural gift for the first disciple in my school is its own matter.
Here it is. I only finished crafting it recently.

After destroying the pursuing Autopuppets, you notice Qingxiao showing signs of Overclocking. Pressed for the truth, she admits she has nearly depleted her Resonance Energy sustaining the Sword Intent she distributed to everyone. She confides the inner turmoil she has been carrying, and you remind her, as you did that one other night, to stay true to the "choice" she made. You decide to stand by her and find a safe place to rest.

You find a relatively safe cabin to rest in. Qingxiao plays her qin to restore her inner balance, but the music only grows more chaotic. When a string finally snaps, the two of you are pulled apart. Alone in the fog-filled cabin, Qingxiao comes face to face with the dead of years past, a manifestation of the inner demon she has yet to overcome. It takes on her likeness and drags her into the depths of her own mind...

You meet Qingxiao's master, Jingwei, who tells you that Qingxiao's struggle with her inner demon has reached its final stage. You are the one Qingxiao has chosen to be her sword. Should the inner demon ever seize control of her, it will fall to you to strike her down.

Again and again, the inner demon insists it is meaningless for Qingxiao to keep helping others, urging her to cut away that part of herself to advance unburdened on the path of cultivation. But for the sake of her true self and the people she protects, Qingxiao chooses to accept her own imperfection and merge with her inner demon. Drawing on its power to replenish her Resonance Energy, she forfeits any chance of transcending and attaining the Way. And yet, in that moment, she finally arrives at the "answer" to the question her master once posed to the heavens.

As Qingxiao wakes, you finally meet within her inner landscape. She has come to understand the path she will walk from here on. She tells you of the Fortress and Gorges War two hundred years ago, and how the two of you once crossed paths at the Gorges of Spirits. Even when aid offers no guarantee of a good end, you will both still follow your hearts and do all you can. In this shared calling to protect, neither of you stands alone. Fellow guardians at heart, you lay yourselves bare to one another, and Qingxiao sets aside her reserve and claims you as her disciple.

You reach the deck of the Sanctum Shuttle and, to your shock, find Muyu's corpse. Yet the disturbance here is still unresolved. While you grapple with the scene, his body suddenly "resurrects." Muyu explains that he resorted to this brute-force method to break the restriction Hsin placed on the Sentinel's knowledge. Your confrontation ends with him collapsing once more, and then, a voice rings out around you...

Muyu, drawing on the Reverberations of the dead from the Di Realm to sustain himself, is pierced through by the Sword Intent radiating from the Autopuppets Qingxiao empowered. As he falls, your questioning draws out his true intent: he came for the Sentinel's knowledge sealed within the Civilization Capsule. While he was willing to destroy the Capsule outright to get it, he claims it was someone else who wanted it intact. He warns you that Xuanfang Hold exists only because the Sentinel meddled in mortal affairs, and that every life it has saved comes at a cost that must eventually be paid. The disturbance now tearing through the Xuanyuan Domain, he says, is simply the destruction Xuanfang was always fated to face.
 
You defeat Muyu, but the "falling sky" unleashed by the Reverberation corruption still looms, and Xuanfang Hold's control kernel is on the verge of collapse.

In a mysterious garden, you and Qingxiao finally meet the long-missing Hsin the Moon Fox. Thanks to everyone's efforts, the crisis has, for now, come to a close. In answer to your questions, Hsin explains how She responded to the chaos Muyu set in motion, and you learn that Xuanfang Hold's control mainframe is actually just a small piece of the Civilization Capsule. As for why She never deployed the Cloud Shuttles or other mechanisms during the Fortress and Gorges War, Hsin says there simply was not enough time, and admits She still isn't sure whether such advanced mechanist arts are a blessing or a curse for Mengzhou, given how much they entangle and reshape people's fates. Before parting, She promises to give you and Xuanfang Hold answers when the time is right. As Hsin's form vanishes, the Rafter Kite that once guided Qingxiao flies into the distance...

Yanshu explains that the Qingfu pendant is the kind Nethermancers carry when entering a Mirage Realm, meaning the Cat of the Nether Lamp's clue likely points to one. Just as Yanshu seems to realize something, Yangyang arrives with the Xuanfang Wardens, bearing bad news: a nearby Censure Court has stopped functioning. The villagers need to be evacuated to Xuanfang Hold immediately. In that moment, Qingxiao looks toward Xuanfang Hold and senses the Celestial Ring Formation gradually grinding to a halt...

A family is tending to a badly wounded Xuanfang Warden who was hurt covering their escape. At a little girl's request, Qingxiao uses her Quietude Art to ease the soldier into peaceful sleep. You notice she seems a little downhearted, aware that her ability cannot take away the soldiers' true pain.

You regroup with the Warden Commander and Yangyang to plan your next move. You suspect something may have gone wrong inside the Sanctum, the home of Xuanfang Hold's control mainframe, and that Muyu's true body could be hiding there, in the one place no one has searched. After discussion, you and Qingxiao are chosen to investigate the Sanctum while Yangyang and the others hold the line around the Ministry of War. Since defenses are not fully in place yet, you will rest for the night and set out the next day. Qingxiao slips away, apparently to make some preparations of her own...

Following the sound of a qin, you find Qingxiao playing in a pavilion near the Ministry of War. She is using the music to distribute protective Sword Intent to Xuanfang's soldiers and civilians as a safeguard. She explains why she arrived late to the earlier crisis: Muyu had set a trap, taking wounded soldiers hostage and forcing her to single-handedly fight off an entire Censure Court while protecting them. Now, with the Land of Xuanfang badly weakened and another crisis looming, Qingxiao cannot help blaming herself. Your words help her let go of her guilt and focus on what she can do now, sharing her Sword Intent with everyone who needs it. Under the bright moon, to the drift of her music, you stay quietly by her side...

The next day, you meet up with Qingxiao and Yangyang at the Ministry of War.
